newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PacDun continues fall after US court ruling.
newsitem.headline: PacDun continues fall after US court ruling.

text.p: The shares of Pacific Dunlop Ltd continued to slide following a U.S. court ruling on Monday which recertified a class comprising U.S. citizens who have been implanted with the company's faulty pacemaker leads.
At 10.15 a.m (0015 GMT), Pacific Dunlop shares were 7.9 cents weaker at A$3.11 after falling 7.1 cents to A$3.189 on Monday.
On Monday, the company said its subsidiary, Accufix Research Institute Inc (ARI), had advised that the U.S. district court in Cincinnati, Ohio, had recertified the class.
The class had previously been decertified in July last year due to problems posed by differing state laws in the U.S. governing each of the common issues certified for trial.
ARI was established after the recall of Accufix "J" pacemaker leads in 1994, the source of the legal action against the company after reports that a wire in the lead could fracture.
About 40,000 such leads were implanted worldwide, 25,000 of them in the United States.
Pacific Dunlop has previously announced a provision of A$85 million for the Institute's costs.

In October last year Pacific Dunlop sold its pacemaker manufacturer, Telectronics to St Jude Medical Inc for A$170 million but retained responsibility for Telectronics products made prior to the sale.
On Monday, Pacific Dunlop said the court's decision did not deal with the merits of the case and did not imply any liability on behalf of ARI.
The company said it was considering the avenues available to it to oppose the certification.
